subtitle: Ten years of war, ten years lost, and strangers eating his home

narrativeBlocks.title: Twenty years gone
narrativeBlocks.body: Odysseus left for Troy when his son Telemachus was a baby. The war ended ten years ago — every other king is home or dead, but no word has come from Ithaca's. On his island, most have stopped believing he will return.

narrativeBlocks.title: Wolves at the table
narrativeBlocks.body: Over a hundred young nobles have moved into his palace — not as guests but as squatters courting his 'widow'. They slaughter his herds for daily feasts, drink his wine, and dare anyone to stop them. Taking Penelope means taking the kingdom.

narrativeBlocks.title: Penelope's loom
narrativeBlocks.body: Penelope cannot refuse outright without a revolt. So she weaves a burial shroud for old Laertes by day — and unravels it by torchlight each night. The trick holds three years before a maid betrays it. Time bought, nothing more.

narrativeBlocks.title: Telemachus comes of age
narrativeBlocks.body: Her son, raised in a house of occupation, finally acts: Athena, disguised, sends him abroad for news of his father — his first command, and the moment he stops being a boy in his own hall.

narrativeBlocks.title: The Odyssey starts at home
narrativeBlocks.body: Unlike the Iliad, this epic opens on the cost of absence — a hero's journey matters because something at home depends on it. Keep the suitors' table in mind: every delay at sea is another feast off Odysseus's stores.
